title: Flat proper finitely presented direct image preserves pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $f:Y\to S$ be a flat proper morphism of finite presentation between schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every pseudo-coherent $E\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], $Rf_*E$ is pseudo-coherent on $S$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. No Noetherian hypothesis or lower cohomological bound on $E$ is imposed.

proof.text: Pseudo-coherence is local on the base by [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For an affine open $V\subseteq S$, [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] identifies $(Rf_*E)|_V$ with $R(f_V)_*(E|_{Y_V})$, where $Y_V=f^{-1}V$. The map $f_V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). It is flat because its source and target stalk maps are the original stalk maps of $f$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Its source is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], since a proper morphism is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Restriction of the local finite-free models makes $E|_{Y_V}$ pseudo-coherent. Thus replace $S,Y,f,E$ by $V,Y_V,f_V,E|_{Y_V}$ for the rest of the argument. This reduction makes $S$ affine and $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated; it imposes no global quasi-compactness on the original $S$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-pseudo-coherent-qcoh], $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Since $f$ is of finite presentation it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-uniform-truncation-bound] on the now affine base to choose a positive integer $N$ such that $H^i(Rf_*A)=0$ for $i\geq N$ whenever $A\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has no positive cohomology. Fix an arbitrary integer $m$, and put $a=m-N-1$. Apply [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-perfect-approximation] to obtain a perfect $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $u:P\to E$ such that $H^i(u)$ is an isomorphism for $i>a$ and $H^a(u)$ is surjective. Neither this approximation theorem nor the uniform bound requires a lower bound on $E$.

source.place: Tag 0CSD, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; expanded approximation proof of Tag 0CSC, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with the structure sheaf in degree zero

proof.text: Complete $u$ to a distinguished triangle $P\to E\to C\to P[1]$ using [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The quasi-coherent subcategory is triangulated by [lem-pc-supported-qcoh-triangulated] with the supporting subset all of $Y$, so $C$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] shows $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\geq a$: for $i=a$ use the surjectivity of $H^a(u)$ and injectivity of $H^{a+1}(u)$, and for $i>a$ use the two adjacent isomorphisms. Consequently $C[a-1]$ has no positive cohomology, with the cochain convention $H^j(C[r])=H^{j+r}(C)$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0CSD, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; expanded approximation proof of Tag 0CSC, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with the structure sheaf in degree zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-proper-support-perfect-direct-image] to $P$ and $\mathcal G^\bullet=\mathcal O_Y[0]$. Its sole nonzero term is finitely presented, having the presentation $0\to\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_Y\to0$; all other terms are zero. It is flat over $S$: at $y$, its stalk is $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, flat over $\mathcal O_{S,f(y)}$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Its support is all of $Y$ (the local ring at a scheme point is nonzero), proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1), using $Y$ itself as a closed subscheme structure. The zero terms have empty support, also proper by part (2). The finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$ is unchanged. Thus $Rf_*(P\otimes^L\mathcal O_Y[0])$ is perfect. The right unitor of [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] identifies this object with $Rf_*P$.

source.place: Tag 0CSD, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; expanded approximation proof of Tag 0CSC, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with the structure sheaf in degree zero

proof.text: Apply the bound from step 2 to $C[a-1]$. The unbounded right derived functor commutes with shifts and preserves distinguished triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Hence $H^j(Rf_*C)=0$ for $j\geq N+a-1=m-2$, in particular for $j\geq m-1$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the image triangle $Rf_*P\to Rf_*E\to Rf_*C\to (Rf_*P)[1]$. For every $i\geq m$, both adjacent groups $H^{i-1}(Rf_*C)$ and $H^i(Rf_*C)$ vanish, so $H^i(Rf_*u)$ is an isomorphism. Explicitly the shift calculation is $H^i(Rf_*(C[a-1]))=H^{i+a-1}(Rf_*C)$, so the threshold in degree $j=i+a-1$ is $N+a-1$.

source.place: Tag 0CSD, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; expanded approximation proof of Tag 0CSC, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with the structure sheaf in degree zero

proof.text: The perfect object $Rf_*P$ is locally represented by a strictly perfect complex by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Compose each local identification with $Rf_*u$. Step 5 gives cohomology isomorphisms in every degree $>m$ and even an isomorphism, hence a surjection, in degree $m$. These are precisely the witnesses that $Rf_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent in [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Since $m$ was arbitrary, the all-$m$ characterization of [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] gives pseudo-coherence. Return through the isomorphisms of step 1 and the affine open covering of the original base. The argument allows empty schemes, zero complexes, non-Noetherian bases, and complexes unbounded below.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-c31cd2cf8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and the statement of every cited node, and checked them against Stacks perfect.tex 0CSC, 0CSE and 0CSD (lines 7457-7568). There is no repair note for this item, so the re-split rules do not apply. The delivery has no new nodes. The statement matches the copy in the O1 snapshot where the node was created and is exactly the pseudo-coherence clause of 0CSD, not weakened. The six steps are the proof of 0CSC with G=O_Y[0] (b=0, so the sigma-truncation paragraph is not needed): (1) 08FE restriction to an affine V; f_V is proper and of finite presentation by base change and flat by stalks; Y_V is qcqs. (2) N from 08D5 and a perfect P approximating E at a=m-N-1 (08ES). (3) The long exact sequence gives H^i(C)=0 for i>=a, so C[a-1] has no positive cohomology. (4) 0A1H applies with G=O_Y[0]: finitely presented, flat over S, support Y proper over S, zero terms with empty support; the unitor gives Rf_*P perfect. (5) H^k(Rf_*C)=0 for k>=m-2, so Rf_*u is an isomorphism in degrees >=m. (6) Composing with local strictly perfect models gives m-pseudo-coherence for every m, then the local definition. I checked the arithmetic, the shift sign and the edge cases (zero or empty, identity map, unbounded-below complexes over non-Noetherian rings, non-quasi-compact base). No duplicates: single-open-pseudo-coherent is about one module, and flat-family-perfect-direct-image-pseudocoherent takes a perfect P under different hypotheses. I accept the seven declared tool_uses as generic coherent and derived-category tools; the other off-unit citations are Mathlib leaves. Batch-5 flag on lem-pc-proper-support-perfect-direct-image: its chain ends in the general definition def-trf-schematically-dense-open, and 0A1H is a coherent finiteness fact that is neither the trace formula, Poincare duality nor a step of their proofs, so the flag is generic. No SGA reference. No changes made.
